auth.notConfigured: Login is not configured yet. Register a public OIDC client and set VITE_BLOCKS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID in .env.
auth.subtitle: Sign in with your Blocks account to continue.
deploy.noRepos.body: Deployment (yml) repositories show only here. Add one with Add repository and tick Deployment repo, or open it on the PRs page and use Mark as deployment repo.
deploy.noRepos.title: No deployment repository yet
deploy.prod.emptyBody: {repo} has no open pull request with 'prod' or 'production' in its title.
deploy.prod.subtitle: Open pull requests in the deployment repository whose title mentions prod or production. Approve and merge run with gh on the runner's machine.
deploy.prod.title: Deploy to prod
deploy.stage.emptyBody: {repo} has no open pull request with 'stage' in its title.

env.dialog.how: Opens a pull request that appends the image to {path}, as your deploy PRs do. Merging it runs the deploy workflow.
env.done.merged: Merged; the deploy workflow is running:
env.done.opened: Pull request opened; approve and merge it on Deploy to stage / prod:
env.drift.aheadHint: This environment runs a newer version than the earlier one (for example a hotfix)
env.drift.behindHint: The earlier environment has newer versions not deployed here yet
env.drift.differsHint: Different images that cannot be ordered
env.footer: Read from the {branch} branch with gh as {account} on runner {runner}. The last line of each file is what runs.
env.mergeNow: Merge right away (deploys {env} now) instead of leaving the pull request for review
env.none.body: The deployment repo has no <service>/dev, stg or production folders with a .txt image list.
env.none.title: No environment files found
env.promote.title: Promote {service} to {to}
env.rollback.title: Roll back {service} on {env}
env.subtitle: What dev, stage and prod run for each service in the deployment repo, how far apart they are, and promote or roll back.
env.title: Environments
profile.subtitle: Signed-in user details from Blocks IAM.
profile.title: Profile
prs.approve.own: GitHub does not let you approve your own pull request.
prs.approve.title: Approve #{number}
prs.col.author: Author
prs.empty.title: No open pull requests
prs.identity: GitHub actions run as {account} with gh on runner {runner}.
prs.merge.draft: Draft pull requests cannot be merged.
prs.merge.notReady: This pull request is not approved or its checks have not all passed. GitHub may refuse the merge if branch protection requires them.
prs.merge.title: Merge #{number}
prs.noRepos.body: Repositories come from KORA runners you may use: the repos in their runner.yml, and ones added here. Add a repository to one of your runners, or start a runner (kora start) whose runner.yml has a repo with a GitHub remote.
prs.noRepos.title: No repositories yet
prs.search.noneBody: Nothing matches “{search}”. Try fewer words, a PR number, or an author.
prs.search.placeholder: Search by #, title, author, branch or label
prs.subtitle: Open pull requests in your runners' repositories. Approve and merge run gh on the runner's machine.
prs.title: Pull requests
quick.koraTooOld: This runner's kora is too old for Quick deploy. Run kora update (0.2.13+) and restart kora start.
quick.title: Quick deploy to {env}
release.col.deployedHint: Build on the merge commit succeeded
release.markDeployed: Mark as deployed (when the build is known to have finished)
release.merge.blocked: Drafts and PRs with conflicts cannot be merged: {prs}. Move them back to Open PRs first.
release.merge.body: Merged in this order, one at a time. After each merge the runner waits until every GitHub Actions run on the merge commit has finished (so each PR gets its own version), then merges the next. A failed build stops the queue.
release.merge.notReady: Not approved or checks not all passing: {prs}. GitHub may refuse these if branch protection requires it, which stops the queue.
release.merge.title: Merge {count} pull request(s)
release.queue.cancelHint: Stops after the pull request it is working on
release.queue.meta: {done} of {total} done · started by {who} on runner {runner} · {method}
release.queue.title: Merge queue
release.queueRunning: A merge queue is already running for this repository.
release.stage.subtitle: Drag pull requests to Ready to stage, then merge them one at a time: each waits for the build on its merge commit before the next. Moving cards changes nothing on GitHub.
release.stage.title: Ready to stage deployment
repoSettings.allowAutoMerge.hint: Let pull requests merge automatically once all requirements are met.
repoSettings.allowMergeCommit.hint: Add all commits from the head branch to the base branch with a merge commit.
repoSettings.allowRebaseMerge.hint: Add all commits from the head branch onto the base branch individually.
repoSettings.allowSquashMerge.hint: Combine all commits from the head branch into a single commit.
repoSettings.allowUpdateBranch: Always suggest updating pull request branches
repoSettings.allowUpdateBranch.hint: Offer to update a pull request branch that is behind its base.
repoSettings.archivedNote: This repository is archived, so its settings cannot be changed.
repoSettings.badTopic: "{topic}" is not a valid topic: lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, up to 50 characters.
repoSettings.defaultBranchNote: Changing the default branch changes the base of new pull requests and what people get when they clone.
repoSettings.deleteBranchOnMerge.hint: Delete a pull request's branch once it is merged.
repoSettings.hasDiscussions.hint: Open forum-style conversations for the community.
repoSettings.hasIssues.hint: Track work and bugs in GitHub Issues.
repoSettings.hasProjects.hint: Plan work with GitHub Projects linked to this repository.
repoSettings.hasWiki.hint: Host documentation in the repository wiki.
repoSettings.hidden: GitHub does not show this setting to the runner's account.
repoSettings.noMergeMethod: Keep at least one merge method allowed.
repoSettings.readOnly: Read-only: the runner's gh account {account} cannot administer this repository. Use a runner whose gh account is a repository admin.
repoSettings.subtitle: GitHub settings of your runners' repositories, read and saved with gh on the runner's machine.
repoSettings.title: Repository settings
repos.add.body: For a repository you don't have cloned, such as the one you deploy from. The runner checks it with gh and saves it in runner.yml. PRs and settings work on it; tasks need a clone.
repos.add.deploymentHint: Shown only on Release > Deploy to stage and Deploy to prod, not on PRs, Repo settings or Ready to stage.
repos.add.invalid: Enter owner/name or a GitHub URL, for example selise/deploy-config.
repos.add.keyPlaceholder: fe, be, ops... defaults to the folder name
repos.add.localBody: A clone already on the runner's machine, like the FE and BE repos kora init sets up. The runner checks the folder, reads its GitHub remote and saves it in runner.yml. Tasks can run on it too.
repos.add.noRemoteNote: This clone has no GitHub remote. Tasks can run on it, but it won't appear on the PRs and Repo settings pages.
repos.add.noRunner: You have no runner online. Run kora start on your machine first; repositories are saved in your runner's runner.yml.
repos.add.noneFound: No new clones found next to your existing ones or in the usual code folders. Type the folder below.
repos.add.scanning: Looking for git folders on the runner...
repos.add.title: Add a repository
repos.markDeployment.hint: Move this repository to Release > Deploy to stage / prod and hide it everywhere else
repos.remove.body: Remove {repo} from runner {runner}? It is taken out of that runner's runner.yml. Nothing changes on GitHub.
repos.remove.title: Remove repository
repos.unmarkDeployment.hint: Move this repository back to PRs, Repo settings and Ready to stage
runners.empty.body: Install KORA, then run kora login, kora init and kora start on a developer machine. It appears here as soon as it connects.
runners.empty.title: No runners online
runners.offline: Could not reach the KORA backend.
runners.subtitle: Developer machines running KORA (kora start), live.
runners.title: Runners
runners.unconfigured.body: This build has no KORA backend address (VITE_KORA_HUB_URL). Runners appear here once the backend is deployed and the web app is rebuilt with its address.
runners.unconfigured.title: KORA backend not connected yet
